title: MetaCan screening label
description: The output contract for one screened work. docs/protocol/rubric.md instructs both machine screeners and both human coders to return exactly this. It did not exist until 2026-07-11 (DEVIATIONS.md D9): the rubric pointed at a file that was not in the repository, and the schema was inlined in the prompts instead. A locked instrument that references a missing file is not locked.

id.description: OpenAlex work ID, bare (W123456789), not the full URL.

tier.description: T1 core metaresearch; T2 adjacent (STS, LIS, research infrastructure); T3 contextual (policy, editorials: mapped, never pooled with T1/T2); OUT otherwise. The in-scope decision that gates the corpus is tier in {T1, T2}. `insufficient_payload` (v2.1) is NOT a screening judgment: it states that the record cannot be screened at all (a scraping artifact as a title, boilerplate in the abstract field, a title and abstract from different papers, spam). It is distinct from OUT and must be REPORTED, not silently dropped: the size of this class is a finding about OpenAlex. Rubric v2.0 mandated this value while this enum could not express it, which is DEVIATIONS.md D20 committed by the document that fixes D20. See D25.

genre.description: OpenAlex `type` is unreliable and this field is commentary-heavy, so genre is screened rather than inherited.

about_ca.description: Is the work ABOUT the Canadian research system, irrespective of author location? This is the secondary estimand (PROTOCOL s3) and is recorded separately from the primary.

confidence.description: The screener's own confidence, as defined in the rubric. QUOTED VERBATIM from rubric v2: "if the abstract is missing, judge on the title alone and set confidence to `low` unless the title is unambiguous." In v1 this gloss PARAPHRASED the rubric as requiring `low` WHENEVER the abstract is missing, which is a different rule; since `low` routes a record to human adjudication and a third of the frame has no abstract, the paraphrase silently changed which records a human ever looks at (DEVIATIONS.md D24). A schema quotes its codebook; it never restates it.

reason.description: Optional. One clause naming the rubric criterion that decided it. Required when confidence is `low` or tier is T2 (the contested boundary).
